body: I put it there for now, inspired by what we do in Satellite, we have a global CSS class `focusable` (`fosauble-visible`, etc...) to keep our focus styles consistent across components.
I took care of adding hover styles when it is supported
I had to duplicate the SVG several times because we can't use `currentColor` for the stroke, so I had to change the stroke color for when it's selected and also for dark mode.

```suggestion
      [class^='ais-'][disabled]
```
Do we prefer that syntax?
should this live in the `reset`?
should we have a variable here instead of defining `#fff`?

I saw that pure white was used in the autocomplete classic theme without a variable, so I went that way.
But we could use something like `--ais-color-white-rgb: 255, 255, 255;`
No strong opinion on this one, WDYT @sarahdayan?
Could there be a case where you would use the class without the actual attribute?

I feel like it should be a variable, just incase the background color is changed for example, white text 
might not work etc.
I'm not sure about that, do you know if it's consistent @sarahdayan?

@FabienMotte I'd imagine it's quite unlikely but thought just throw it out there.

Could we have multiple variants of the selector to cover _potential_ edge cases?
I agree, done!
Can be argued, but this ruleset is about disabling opinionated styles in themes, not about resetting browser defaults, so common sounds fine.
Sounds great! Let's just make sure it doesn't clash with the focus style for the search box.
We _should_ have the `disabled` attribute present on all show more buttons. If we realize it isn't the case we can always fix it in InstantSearch, it's not breaking and is actually a good fix.
Can we have an internal variable?
Should we use a more semantic naming? If customers want to customize it, it's weird to set `--ais-color-white-rgb` to a different color.
Thanks for the feedback, I'll go with `[disabled]` then
Let's keep it in `common.css`
It should only be present when you use the keyboard to navigate on the page
I agree, I updated it to `--ais-button-text-color-rgb`, do you have a more generic name maybe?

Good idea! I also added a comment at the top of each one to let us know what color it uses.
And I updated the `stroke-width` to `1.6`.
